public_ownership_contract: Public Call strongly retains its Client until Call GC, including zero-output, pending and completed Calls. Releasing every output does not release the independent Call owner.
OutputFuture and RemoteRef aliases share an owner cell. The unreleased cell strongly retains Client; release invalidates all that cell aliases and clears the cell Client edge in finally.
Public Graph is the existing independent Client owner. Workflow Call._graph remains a legitimate graph-binding capability while that public Call exists; no Graph architecture change.
Explicit Client.close and async context exit revoke network/session resources even while Calls/cells/Graphs remain. Local completed metadata may remain as tombstones; remote operations fail.
State/client_ref, invocation lifetime, state.cells, ready_ref and call_ref remain weak. Finalizer arguments remain weak Client plus pure wire record; no Cell/State in callback registry.

After the last public owner disappears, GC stops the keeper and schedules normal transport/session disposal. Whole-session close/TTL may subsume individual release messages; no per-output release ordering promise.
Borrowed output handles retain session capability but do not pin native cache. Native cache eviction still yields Expired and does not recreate/recompute the producer.

internal_scheduling_contract.weak_gc_controls: release_info and forget_call enqueue module weak-method dispatch with only wire data; queued callbacks cannot become another session owner
internal_scheduling_contract.fresh_contexts: SDK-owned tasks, internal Task/Future done callbacks, GC scheduling, keeper notifications/watch/cancel, and keeper OS thread construction/start all use fresh contextvars.Context
internal_scheduling_contract.legitimate_user_context: User active fetch/close/await execution, user tasks and user-registered callbacks are untouched. The user-requested close task keeps caller context; only its SDK exception-retrieval callback is isolated.
internal_scheduling_contract.context_policy_basis: No prior public API or documentation promised app ContextVars propagation into long-lived SDK internal tasks; copying arbitrary Client/Graph values caused real hidden owners. No ContextVar blacklist or new framework introduced.
internal_scheduling_contract.runtime_boundary: Actual supported-environment validation is Python3.11/3.12. No runtime claim for newer inheriting-thread builds; public Context.run wraps both Thread construction and start without version branches.
